title: Evaluate dependent multi-shift nullities by exact convolution
body:
This algorithmic improvement evaluates the existing joint-nullity law for distinct scalar shifts by exact convolution. For one nullity vector, with m=n-sum(a_i), the cost is O(n+t(m+1)^2) arithmetic operations, with O(m) live coefficients and O(n) factorial values. It replaces binomial(m+t,t) feasible dimension tuples. This makes dependent shifted-rank counts cheaper to evaluate. It does not improve the complete kappa calculation or supply a paid Schur-header cover.

The [proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1f1ea775d1d67800f29e28d7c2d174fb34964b05/research/multishift-nullity-convolution/PROOF.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1f1ea775d1d67800f29e28d7c2d174fb34964b05/research/multishift-nullity-convolution/RESULT.json), [timing receipt](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1f1ea775d1d67800f29e28d7c2d174fb34964b05/research/multishift-nullity-convolution/BENCHMARK.json) and [source manifest](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1f1ea775d1d67800f29e28d7c2d174fb34964b05/research/multishift-nullity-convolution/SOURCES.json) define the claim. The proof covers all prime powers, dimensions and sets of distinct shifts. Arithmetic counts do not bound integer bit costs. At q=17,n=24,t=17, the algorithm uses 5525 coefficient products; the direct formula has 151584480450 summands. That large direct reference was not run.

Base: canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority revision 7. @petalas supplied the two-shift law and finite-field arithmetic in [PR #4803](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4803). The Schur application is credited there to ssafwann's [PR #4678](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4678). Ali Romman's existing [multi-shift Discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5261) supplies the formula being accelerated. Its consumed text is [retained here](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1f1ea775d1d67800f29e28d7c2d174fb34964b05/research/multishift-nullity-convolution/DISCUSSION-5261.md). Gaussian inversion and generating functions are classical; no external mathematical priority is claimed.

With CPython 3.12 and no third-party packages, from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/multishift-nullity-convolution
python3.12 -I -B research/multishift-nullity-convolution/benchmark.py
```

Expected verifier status: `PASS_MULTISHIFT_CONVOLUTION_NO_NEW_KAPPA`. Normal and optimized CPython 3.12.13, optimized 3.14.7, committed-byte checks, the official 14-file export and a Git-free optimized replay passed. Source and receipt corruption were rejected. The verifier checks 2821 direct-formula comparisons, 21805 matrices in 11 contexts including F4, 481 nullity bins, three full-distribution/marginal contexts and eleven controls. Five alternating benchmark runs at q=7,n=12,t=7 gave identical counts and a 547.18x median speedup on the stated host; this is a local measurement, not a universal timing guarantee.

An actual nonbinary producer weight, paid selection/emission, physical reads, restoration and complete supplier pricing remain open. No Lean, Docker, native admission, selected cold replay or independent human/proof-kernel review was run. Optional full-history verification is unavailable in this shallow checkout. The selected frontier is unchanged. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.
